Maya R: Heads-up: possible perf regression when enabling flash+paged fusion on long-context evals. Can someone run a 32k-seq microbench on main vs release/2026-02? CI showed ~15% drop on a couple of runs and we need A100/H100 numbers to triage.

Theo K: Sure. Which model + exact command + queue?

Maya R: llama-2-13b, bf16, batch=1. Example command: `./bench.sh --model llama-2-13b --seq 32768 --b 1 --mode flash_paged --iters 10`. Use perf-long (A100/80GB) and perf-h100. Record p50 throughput and peak GPU memory.

Jamal S: I can run on perf-h100 in ~30m. Any env vars or runtime specifics?

Maya R: Use torch 2.2.0+cu121, runtime branch: compare `main` vs tag `release/2026-02`. Set `export TF32=0` and `export RCCL_SYNC=false` to reduce NCCL noise we saw.

Priya N: Also make sure to enable `--kv-cache-optim true` and `--disable-prefetch false` so the run mirrors prod. Please also run seq=16384 as a control.

perf-bot: Quick run summary (perf-h100, batch=1):
- main: 11.2 tok/s, peak_mem 38.1 GB
- release/2026-02: 13.1 tok/s, peak_mem 36.5 GB
Raw logs: /bench/logs/1789954321/{main,release}.out

Theo K: Oof. Can you paste a kernel-time breakdown? Might be falling back to non-fused path or increased memcpy.

Jamal S: Pasting top kernel profile from the H100 run (nvprof style):
```
kernel_name           time_ms
flash_attn_fused      46.2
flash_attn_paged      58.9
kv_cache_write        4.8
memcpy_h2d            3.1
```

Maya R: That matches what we feared — paged path is ~25% slower in hot kernel. @eng-runtime can we bisect between the two commits that touched kernel selection (the PR that introduced the paged fallback last month)? If someone can pin the PR/commit we can check where the regression comes from.

Theo K: :thumbsup: I'll start a git bisect tomorrow on the perf-h100 pool. If anyone has a suspected commit hash, drop it here to speed things up.

Priya N: Also re-assigning PERF-412 to this thread and adding a note to run the short/long seq comparison.

Maya R: Thanks — please paste any short logs or kernel diffs here. If bisect points to a runtime heuristic change, we can either revert or add a config flag to force the fused path until we fix the paged kernel.

Jamal S: Will upload full nvprof + run script to /bench/artifacts/1789954321 by EOD.

perf-bot: Scheduled: perf-h100 run queued (job 7892). ETA ~45m.

Theo K: If bisect is noisy, I’ll try disabling prefetch or toggling `KV_CACHE_OPTIM` to see if it's an ordering/placement regression rather than pure kernel perf.

Maya R: Perfect. Thanks all — keeping this thread as the single source for results.
